newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bigger job cuts planned at E.German SKET - Spiegel.
newsitem.headline: Bigger job cuts planned at E.German SKET - Spiegel.

text.p: Troubled east German machinery company Sket GmbH will have to cut more jobs than originally planned, leaving the company with just 400 employees instead of the proposed 570, German news magazine Der Spiegel reported.
Sket, which once employed 18,000 workers as a main supplier to communist eastern Europe, has soaked up billions in state aid after posting heavy losses since German unification.

In mid-October, the firm filed for liquidation proceedings after its workforce, already reduced to 1,850 reflecting the company's troubles, refused to support a drastic cost-cutting programme which would have cut the workforce by two-thirds.
The company's troubles made headline news in Germany, with the Bonn government coming under fire from the opposition Social Democrat Party for going back on promises to save SKET.

According to the Spiegel report, a rescue plan for SKET agreed at the start of this week between Wolfgang Wutzke, the lawyer charged with handling the liquidation of SKET, and the BVS state agency will split five core areas of the company into separate shell operating groups.

Of the total workforce of 1,850, only 400 would then remain in the company, with 200 trainees, the plan said. The rest of the workforce would be transferred to a company which would aim to find and create new jobs for them, it said.
The BvS declined to confirm or deny the report. "The ink is not dry yet," a spokesman said. "We hope that we will be able to come to an agreement soon."
